hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/mb/mb_model MBOX_BGLoadModelStart 0x0:0x30 --diff` at head e5eb50945 shows target `14: addi r29,r5,0 @lbl_80115DA8(ADDR16_LO)` and `24: addi r28,r5,0 @lbl_802A5CF0(ADDR16_LO)` against our `24: mr r28,r0` and `28: addi r29,r5,0 @lbl_802A5CF0(ADDR16_LO)`; the transposition is read off the target bytes, not inferred.
hypothesis.statement: Our build's callee-saved homes for the two prologue addresses are TRANSPOSED against the target - target homes lbl_80115DA8 in r29 and lbl_802A5CF0 in r28 (`addi r29,r5,DA8@lo` at +0x14, `addi r28,r5,CF0@lo` at +0x24), ours homes them r28 and r29 respectively - and probe B proves declaration order cannot swap them because both locals are the same width class. The remaining carrier of callee-saved numbering for same-width locals is therefore something other than declaration order, and whatever it is also decides which of the two addresses is forced through r0: in ours it is the one homed to the LOWER register (r28), in the target the lower register (r28) is homed directly. The next lane should identify the same-width numbering carrier before spending any further probe on the copy.
